title: A pointer token matches a key that carries a local tag by its text
notes: A pointer token matches a mapping key by the key's scalar text (docs/edit-semantics.md, Refusals), and a tag does not change a scalar's text. The key is the only one whose text is `foo`, so the edit is not ambiguous and writes onto its value; no second key is added. In YAML 1.2.2 section 3.2.1.3 a key tagged `!local` is a different node from the plain string `foo`, which matters for a library that looks keys up by value in its own data model (a dictionary lookup of the string `foo` does not find it) but not for a pointer, which is text. The exact bytes rest on a kit convention.

provenance.reference: Found in oneyaml-python: setting the string key `foo` by value (not by pointer) added a plain key beside the tagged one in the native backend and wrote onto the tagged key in the pure backend. A value lookup and a pointer differ here by design; a pointer reaches the tagged key in both backends, which this case pins.
